stem: You are opening the airway of a 5-month-old infant during paediatric basic life support; which position is recommended?

options.text: Neutral position with a towel under the shoulders

explanation: Neutral position with a towel under the shoulders is the recommended airway position for an infant during paediatric basic life support. This helps maintain an open airway without overextending the neck.

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because full neck extension can obstruct the infant airway and is not recommended.
optionExplanations.B: Correct because infants should have the airway opened in a neutral position, and a towel under the shoulders can help achieve this.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because the sniffing position is used for older children, not young infants.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because Trendelenburg position is not used to open the infant airway in basic life support.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because sitting upright is not the recommended airway-opening position in infant paediatric basic life support.
